content:
I use for hiking - this app can transform your world.

The information and guidance with 5 mins planning and research can quick turn you in to a local expert. 

Pick the right shoes, clothing, hydration , snacks , bring a battery will take you into the very best that Mother Nature can offer. 

It’s a great way to build and maintain fitness  and see the best of each season.  Use on your doorstep or on holiday- the GPS means you will never get lost.

title: Immediate subscription? No.
content:
This app might be good, but immediately and repeatedly after downloading, it pushes to subscribe on a trial basis for access to anything beyond the absolute most basic information. Asking people to subscribe before they even know what they’re subscribing to is a business model that amounts to, “We hope you forget you subscribed.” To be fair, they might not actually intend that, but it sure feels that way.

UPDATE: The developer responded with, “but we offer a free trial.” Um, yes, I mentioned that prominently. But without a free tier of substance, there’s no way to assess the app even a little bit without subscribing. Free trials are too easily forgotten and seven days is an unreasonably short period for assessment. If you’re a hard-core hiker, going for ten-mile hikes every single day and constantly thinking about hiking—and one’s hiking app—a seven day trial might work. But normal people who have other stuff on their minds are gonna forget to unsubscribe.

It was great for finding a new route in my local area. There were plenty of options which I was able to filter to be mid or dog friendly and I could see basic info such as length, difficulty and a brief description which even helped me to decide which pram to bring (the off-roader, based on the description’s recommendations for a “robust” pram).

All of the info was accurate. So far, so good. 

I did encounter some issues recording the walk in app though. Firstly, the Apple Watch app stopped recording 3 seconds into the walk, and nothing I could do would fix it. I later found that this was recorded as a duplicate activity which I was able to delete. Presumably this happened when I lowered my wrist after checking my watch immediately at the start of the walk and I’ve noticed that unless I have the app open on my watch and my wrist raised, it does not get detected by the phone app, which directs me to install the watch app. 

I was also disappointed to find that despite me allowing the app to write all requested activity data to Apple Health including workouts and granting location access, no location or route data, nor elevation, splits or weather information, was saved to the Health/Fitness app, and active and total calorie values were incorrectly identical as well, so the data for AllTrails sessions is much less robust than those saved by the Workouts app on my Watch.

title: Immediate subscription? No.
content:
This app might be good, but immediately and repeatedly after downloading, it pushes to subscribe on a trial basis for access to anything beyond the absolute most basic information. Asking people to subscribe before they even know what they’re subscribing to is a business model that amounts to, “We hope you forget you subscribed.” To be fair, they might not actually intend that, but it sure feels that way.

UPDATE: The developer responded with, “but we offer a free trial.” Um, yes, I mentioned that prominently. But without a free tier of substance, there’s no way to assess the app even a little bit without subscribing. Free trials are too easily forgotten and seven days is an unreasonably short period for assessment. If you’re a hard-core hiker, going for ten-mile hikes every single day and constantly thinking about hiking—and one’s hiking app—a seven day trial might work. But normal people who have other stuff on their minds are gonna forget to unsubscribe.

title: Does the job, but there’s room for improvement.
content:
The map function is great and I love having a space just to record my hikes. Two suggestions:

- I paid for an annual membership just so I could get my downloaded map on my watch. The need to constantly pull my phone out to check my location was very inconvenient. Very disappointed. 
- it would be great if at a certain zoom I could start seeing the trails get highlighted on a map (the way physical maps and ski maps do, with trails marked in different colours etc), and when I select that trail I could see the suggested hikes associated with it. Selecting a pin with 12 hikes, each small variations of each other, and not having an easy way to compare the difference between them is very clunky. 

Thank you and I hope the app will get better! I love hiking and would love to support a community designed for hikers 😊

title: Overpriced and buggy.  No ipad.
content: For the ridiculously high subscription price they charge and constantly constantly constantly try to get you to buy, the app is poor.  It’s 2025 as I write this.. there is zero excuse zero.. for not having an iPad version.  The actual app is OK, but within my first hike in extremely popular chamonix I found many incorrect and missing trails and also the AllTrails map was very misleading as to where many trails go.  Finally, a huge bug… it seems the app is listing a certain contour elevations in feet numbers, but using M to indicate meters.  In short, I expect more than such amateur hour nonsense from an app which charges so much and whose makers have made millions and millions and millions in profit.  Embarrassingly bad.   Oh, and to say nothing of the fact that while I use the iPhone version all day yesterday, I just started this on iPad now.  I decided to investigate some trails today.  I started the map mode and not left my bed while checking it out and writing this review.  However, all trails has somehow already logged that i have walked 0.37 km.  Highly highly highly suspect app.  Alternatives are available both free and paid that are better than this overrated rubbish.
